html:
SMTO-SKL-0098 — Replacing a OneDrive file needs its current version first

GUID: 8c8b2571-3a7f-5f98-bc9b-f7f9033079bc
Slug: microsoft365-precondition-required
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • You asked to replace a file that already exists. SMTO only replaces a file after it has checked which version is there now, so nothing was uploaded.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to show the details of the existing file you want to replace. This lets SMTO see exactly which version you are about to overwrite.
  2. Then ask the Agent to replace that file with your new one. With the current version known, the replacement can go ahead safely.
  3. If you don't want to overwrite it, ask the Agent to upload your file under a different name instead. A new name avoids replacing anything at all.

What success looks like

  • The Agent reports the upload as complete and OneDrive shows your new file.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • microsoft365 file_upload was called with conflict=replace but no etag, so the upload was refused before any request was sent.

What this means

  • File upload selects conflict=replace without supplying an ETag. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • File upload selects conflict=replace without supplying an ETag.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect conflict mode and the target item's current ETag.

How to fix it

  • Call microsoft365.file_info (or file_list) for the exact target item, then repeat file_upload with conflict=replace and etag set to the observed eTag. Without an explicit replace, the default conflict=fail keeps existing content intact.
  • Read the target item and supply its observed ETag before replacing existing file content.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate replacement carries the observed exact precondition.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
